strengths: Addresses genuine reproducibility crisis in audio SSL by identifying why SOTA results cannot be reproduced (e.g., SSLAM's 40.9 mAP) and providing honest re-implementation with detailed hyperparameters

CGP is well-motivated and effective: substantially outperforms Protobin (41.04 vs 32.58 mAP on AS-2M for EAT) by combining layer-weighted aggregation with prototypical probing, meaningfully closing frozen evaluation-fine-tuning gap
Comprehensive ablations isolating each component's contribution (data preprocessing, gated attention, decoder architecture) with clear interpretability through layer-wise analysis (Figure 4)

Excellent experimental rigor: new PyTorch implementation avoiding legacy fairseq code, detailed hyperparameter specification (Appendix A), evaluation across four benchmarks with consistent improvements, and promises code release

Solid technical execution: clear presentation, well-designed figures, honest reporting of both successes and failures, practical focus on frozen-feature evaluation for resource-constrained practitioners

Principled architectural choices with clear motivations (local normalization improves robustness and deployment, gated attention addresses attention sinks, larger decoder shifts semantics to final layers)
weaknesses: Limited novelty: CGP extends prototypical probing with straightforward softmax-weighted layer aggregation; gated attention is borrowed from Qiu et al. (2025); individual improvements are mostly engineering (normalization, larger decoder)

Incomplete resolution of fine-tuning problem: CGP still shows substantial gaps (5.65pp on AS-2M, 3.8pp on AS-20k) despite claims of 'faithful evaluation' replacing fine-tuning; the fundamental issue isn't solved, only measured better

Modest fine-tuning gains: BAT achieves only ~1pp improvement over EAT, and neither approaches reported numbers (48.6 EAT vs 48.55 BAT), raising questions about practical significance and reproducibility despite framing as SOTA

Unclear generalization: all experiments on AudioSet variants; unknown whether CGP, gated attention, and architectural choices transfer to other domains (music, speech-specific tasks, other audio modalities); acknowledged but unexplored

Generalization of semantic information shift not established: the shift of task-relevant information to later layers (Figure 4c) is shown for BAT but may be architecture-dependent or dataset-specific rather than universally beneficial

Reproducibility challenges remain despite claims: inability to reproduce SSLAM and discrepancies in EAT (reported 48.6, reproduced 47.61) suggest deep learning reproducibility is fundamentally difficult; honest but concerning for claims of 'standardized methodology'

Terminology and decomposition issues: 'Convex' in CGP is misleading (softmax creates convex combination but method doesn't solve convex optimization); contributions split between methodology (CGP) and engineering (BAT) makes scope unclear

strengths: Addresses a genuine problem in audio SSL evaluation methodology with well-motivated solution
Thorough experimental work with systematic ablations clearly isolating individual contributions (preprocessing, gated attention, decoder)
Honest discussion of reproducibility challenges and new PyTorch implementation addressing legacy code issues
Consistent improvements across multiple benchmarks (AS-2M, AS-20k, ESC-50, SC-2) in frozen settings
Excellent visualizations justifying design choices (Figures 3-5) and clear presentation overall
Comprehensive hyperparameter documentation and dataset descriptions supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited novelty: CGP is primarily Protobin (Rauch et al., 2025a) with softmax gating borrowed from concurrent LLM work (Qiu et al., 2025); BAT is Data2Vec 2.0 with standard engineering improvements (preprocessing, gated attention, larger decoder)
Disconnected contributions: Title suggests CGP 'guides' BAT development, but most improvements are orthogonal to CGP insights, suggesting these should be separate papers
Persistent gap to fine-tuning undermines core claims: 3.8 pp gap on AS-20k (37.52 vs 41.32 mAP) and 5.65 pp on AS-2M (42.90 vs 48.55), questioning whether CGP offers a faithful alternative
Cannot fully reproduce prior work: SSLAM reproduction off by ~1 pp (reported 40.9, obtained 39.97), raising concerns about fair comparison and valid baselines

Insufficient justification of key design choices: why 10k prototypes (large memory overhead), why this gate placement, why equal loss weighting; large unexplained gap between linear probing (25.59) and CGP (37.52)
Limited scope and generalization: audio-specific work with no evidence insights generalize to vision/language; specialized domain limits impact reach
Missing theoretical foundation: no principled justification for why softmax-gated aggregation is optimal or when CGP should approximate fine-tuning

Incomplete analysis: no computational cost comparison between CGP and fine-tuning, no investigation of when/why CGP works, confounded improvements in decoder ablation (Table 4) mixing capacity and architecture changes

strengths: Addresses reproducibility crisis in audio SSL with concrete evidence (SSLAM 40.9→39.97 mAP non-reproducibility) and proposes practical CGP evaluation method that substantially closes probing-to-fine-tuning gap (8.6pp→5.1pp improvement over Protobin)

Comprehensive evaluation across four benchmarks with systematic ablations (Tables 2-4) isolating each contribution, plus detailed visualization of layer-wise information distribution revealing how decoder capacity affects semantic information location

Strong focus on reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters (Appendix A), clear experimental protocols, resource information, and promised code release. Honest reporting of inability to reproduce prior work rather than overselling results

Well-presented paper with clear motivation flowing logically from problem identification to evaluation method to model improvements. Effective use of figures (especially Figure 3-4) to illustrate preprocessing differences and layer information distribution
weaknesses: Limited novelty: CGP extends Protobin incrementally with softmax layer aggregation; gated attention directly borrowed from Qiu et al. (2025) LLM work without audio-specific validation; ViT decoder is existing technique; preprocessing uses standard signal processing. Each component sensible but individually not novel

Modest performance gains: BAT fine-tuning (41.32 mAP) improves only ~1pp over reproduced EAT (40.28) on primary benchmark—within typical hyperparameter tuning noise. Main improvements appear to derive from baseline reproduction rather than BAT-specific advances

Narrow experimental scope: evaluated only on Data2Vec 2.0-derived models (EAT, SSLAM); no testing on other recent audio SSL methods (BEATs, SSAST) or architectures beyond ViT-Base, limiting generalizability of CGP and BAT claims

Key claims insufficiently validated: (1) Attention gating mechanism explanation borrowed from LLMs lacks audio-specific evidence; Table 3 shows empirical gain but not the proposed mechanism. (2) Removing 8×10⁴ loss scaling improves reproducibility, but paper doesn't investigate why this factor was originally needed, potentially masking rather than solving underlying issues. (3) Figure 2 shows prototype count is dataset-dependent, yet 10k used uniformly without cross-validation

Fundamental tension: Paper argues fine-tuning is unreliable and non-reproducible (Table 1), yet uses fine-tuning as primary evaluation metric and measures CGP success by proximity to fine-tuning results. ~3.8pp gap between CGP (37.52) and fine-tuning (41.32) on AS-20k remains substantial despite reproducibility concerns

Missing technical comparisons: No empirical comparison with mentioned layer-aware methods (VQT, Side-Tuning); no ablation isolating contributions (loss scaling vs. other changes); ESC-50 anomaly (CGP 95.80 > FT 95.52) unexplained, raising probe calibration questions

strengths: Addresses a genuine problem in audio SSL evaluation methodology—the reliance on finetuning obscures progress and reproducibility
Comprehensive experimental validation across 7 downstream tasks with extensive ablations (Tables 2-4) systematically justifying each design choice
Proposes CGP as a practical improvement over prior prototypical probing (ProtoBin) with consistent gains across diverse tasks in Table 5
Provides valuable reproducibility contributions: identifies non-reproducible results in prior work (EAT/SSLAM), offers detailed hyperparameters, and commits to open-source implementations
Insightful visualization of task-relevant information distribution via learned gating weights (Figures 4-5, Appendix F) demonstrating where semantic features concentrate
Well-presented work with clear writing, effective figures, and comprehensive related work positioning audio SSL in broader SSL context
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: CGP is an incremental extension of ProtoBin (adding softmax gating), gated attention is directly borrowed from Qiu et al. (2025) without audio-specific justification, and ViT decoder is a standard architectural choice
Overclaimed gap closure: Table 1 shows CGP still has substantial gaps to finetuning (5+ mAP points on AS-20k), contradicting the claim of 'significantly closing the gap'

Reproducibility concerns about BAT itself: Different loss functions between ablations (binary cross-entropy vs. asymmetric loss), AS-2M sampling sensitivity, and acknowledged hyperparameter tuning requirements in Appendix F undermine the central reproducibility argument

Lack of statistical rigor: No significance testing on main results, standard deviations only for some metrics, and small datasets (e.g., SED with 44 training samples) without confidence intervals or multiple seed validation

CGP design choices insufficiently justified: Why 10k prototypes (Figure 2 shows diminishing returns but no ablation of alternatives)? Why min-max pooling specifically? No ablation on alternative gating mechanisms or pooling strategies

Incomplete experimental analysis: Why does gated attention specifically benefit audio? How does CGP generalize beyond ViT? Comparison fairness concerns (CGP-based evaluation favors CGP-friendly models). Shift in loss functions between ablations (BCE) and final benchmarks (asymmetric loss) is unexplained
Incremental performance improvements: 1-2 mAP point gains per component, with marginal cumulative improvements limiting practical significance despite SOTA positioning

Limited scope and generalization: All work restricted to spectrogram-based ViT models; transferability to other architectures and pretraining datasets unclear; gains may not generalize beyond current setup

strengths: Addresses genuine reproducibility issues in audio SSL with concrete evidence that reported SOTA results cannot be reproduced
Comprehensive evaluation across 7 datasets and 7 probing methods with detailed hyperparameters and promised code release
Systematic ablations clearly decomposing contributions of preprocessing, gated attention, and decoder components
Honest discussion of limitations and reproduction failures, providing value to the community despite not fully solving the reproducibility problem
weaknesses: Limited novelty: CGP is an incremental extension of Protobin (adding softmax gating); gated attention borrowed directly from recent LLM work (Qiu et al. 2025); ViT decoder vs CNN decoder is standard from vision; primarily engineering rather than methodological contribution

Overstated claims about 'closing the gap': Table 1 shows persistent 5+ percentage point gaps between CGP probing and finetuning (e.g., 40.28 vs 35.20 mAP for EAT on AS-20k), contradicting claims of faithful evaluation and significant gap closure

Fundamental reproducibility issues unresolved: Cannot reproduce baseline results even with original code; attributes this to legacy sampling but doesn't fix it, raising concerns about whether BAT improvements come from better methodology or metric overfitting

Unfair experimental comparison: BAT developed and ablated exclusively under CGP metric (Tables 3-4), while baselines optimized for finetuning then re-evaluated on new metric; inconsistent setups (AS-20k + BCE for ablations, AS-2M + A-BCE for final eval)

Weak mechanistic understanding: Paper shows CGP works better empirically but provides no theoretical justification or analysis of *why*; Figure 4 reveals where information concentrates but not why CGP discovers this better; no ablations of CGP components themselves (e.g., pooling strategy, gating mechanism)

Unclear improvement attribution: Largest gains come from ViT decoder (~2 mAP), which is least novel and borrowed from prior vision work; incremental contributions from preprocessing (~0.17 mAP) and attention gating (~0.39 mAP) are modest; no isolation of CGP's specific contribution to final SOTA performance

Limited scope and generality: Audio-specific evaluation only, despite citing vision probing methods; CGP never tested on vision despite claiming general applicability; findings may not generalize to future SSL approaches

Missing critical ablations and analyses: No ablations on CGP itself; no statistical significance testing (only 2 of 7 datasets have error bars); no failure mode analysis or cross-validation; limited exploration of hyperparameter sensitivity beyond documentation

strengths: Addresses critical reproducibility problem in audio SSL evaluation with compelling evidence that finetuning-based SOTA reports may reflect hyperparameter tuning rather than representation quality
Comprehensive evaluation across 7 datasets and 6 different probing methods demonstrates thorough empirical validation and strong SOTA results
Substantial improvements in bridging the frozen-feature probing and finetuning gap (e.g., CGP 35.20 vs linear probing 17.95 for EAT on AS-20k)
Commits to reproducibility through native PyTorch implementation, removal of heuristic loss-scaling, extensive hyperparameter documentation, and promised code release

Thoughtful technical contributions with complete ablations: gated attention addresses attention sinks, better decoder improves encoder utilization, refined preprocessing maintains dataset independence
Insightful analysis of layer-wise semantic information distribution (Figure 4, Appendix F) with strong correlation between CGP gating weights and linear probing performance
Clear presentation with well-designed figures, honest limitations discussion, and transparent comparison with prior SOTA models including identified discrepancies
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: CGP is an incremental extension of Protobin adding learnable soft-gating (weighted averaging), gated attention is directly borrowed from Qiu et al. (2025) for LLMs, better decoder follows He et al. (2022) vision findings; contributions are primarily application rather than methodological innovation

Conceptual tension in 'faithfulness' claims: both finetuning and CGP are evaluated against embeddings themselves, creating circular reasoning; CGP still shows substantial gaps from finetuning (35.20 vs 40.28), suggesting they measure different properties rather than one being objectively superior

Reproducibility claims only partially realized: despite standardization, authors cannot reproduce published results exactly (Table 1: reported 40.2 vs reproduced 40.28 for EAT); AS-2M sampling issues indicate fundamental rather than documentation problems

Critical ablation missing: removal of 8×10⁴ loss-scaling heuristic is drastic change but lacks controlled ablation; unclear how much improvement stems from this vs. architectural modifications, confounding BAT contribution attribution

Statistical rigor gaps: inconsistent error bar reporting across datasets, no significance testing for most comparisons, modest improvements on some benchmarks (1.2 pp on AS-20k finetuning), no stability analysis across random seeds

Insufficient theoretical justification for CGP design: why is soft-gating + prototypes + min-max pooling optimal? Method still requires choosing K prototypes; computational cost significant (3.9G MACs vs 0.0004G for LP) with limited efficiency analysis
Confounded ablations: Table 3 comparisons of MLP vs. EOB targets entangled with gating choice; not fully orthogonal isolation of individual effects

Analysis gaps on failure modes: CGP performance drops substantially on HSN (F1 29.49 vs 34.07 finetuning) without investigation; other methods (VQT, H2T) also underperform on certain tasks without diagnostic analysis
